audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven whys said Ambessa owns the stage while the row above them (both phases[N].side and win[N]) said Warwick or Skill: whys[2] 'favours Ambessa' vs Warwick, whys[3] 'stay hers' vs Skill, whys[4] "Ambessa's" vs Skill, whys[5] 'she leads' vs Warwick, whys[6] 'Ambessa dominates' vs Warwick.
audit.why: Packet defect confirms it: Warwick wins 60.9% over 752 games but the prose gives Ambessa five stages. The sides are the number-backed layer, so the prose is what is wrong.
audit.corrected: whys[2] through whys[6], plus the four spikes, early, mid and late rewritten to the side each row actually holds. Sides untouched — full and content already agree row for row.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown anywhere, and Ambessa's spike was described only as 'her kit online'.
audit.why: Public Execution is 130s at rank 1 — the longest window in the lane and the thing to fight around. Lacerate 13s, Cunning Sweep 14s, Jaws of the Beast down to 7s.
audit.corrected: 130s Public Execution written into spikes[1], phases[4].why and mid; Lacerate's 13s and Q's 7s into whys[2] and whys[3]; Blood Hunt's 50%/25% thresholds into spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: not one Ambessa ability is named anywhere — the entry invents 'Repeating Dashes' for her whole kit. Infinite Duress is called point-and-click. And the passive is pointed the wrong way, exactly as the mirror found: 'let the passive out-heal his return damage' implies constant sustain.
audit.why: Riot's text: Eternal Hunger heals only when Warwick is under 50% health, tripled under 25%. Infinite Duress is a directional leap that suppresses the FIRST champion it collides with, so Drakehound's Step cannot dodge it once it is travelling. Cunning Sweep transforms into Sundering Slam only after it strikes an enemy — that is the real sequencing tell.
audit.corrected: Cunning Sweep, Sundering Slam, Repudiation, Lacerate, Drakehound's Step and Public Execution named; the Q-transform tell stated in spikes[0]; the passive corrected to key off your own health in tradeGood, mid and late; R restated as a collision leap.

notes: Two systemic errors here. (1) The whole prose layer said Ambessa wins levels 3 through late while the chart rows and a 60.9% win rate over 752 games say otherwise — the packet flags this defect explicitly. Rewrote the prose to the chart, not the chart to the prose. (2) The mirror's finding reproduces here: Eternal Hunger was written as if it out-heals incoming damage generally. It only heals when Warwick himself is under 50%, tripled under 25% — that inverts the trading plan, and it is worth sweeping every other Warwick matchup for the same sentence. Also: the entry names no Ambessa ability at all, inventing 'Repeating Dashes'; that phrase survives in focus.text, loading, and many report/breakdown strings I could not safely rewrite within the length band (see questions).
